question.text: Under the Reverse Mortgage Scheme in India, a senior citizen can:

answer.text: Sell their residential property to a bank and continue living in it
Receive regular payments from a bank by mortgaging their residential property while continuing to live in it
Transfer property ownership to children in exchange for monthly payments
Take a personal loan against movable assets like gold and securities

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p187-188, a senior citizen pledges (mortgages) the residential property to a financial institution and receives periodic income, while continuing to own and reside in the property. The Trap: Option A describes a sale, not a mortgage — ownership remains with the senior citizen in a reverse mortgage loan (RML). Note: Per p187-188, the RML becomes due when the last surviving borrower dies or moves out; sale proceeds are used to settle the loan, any surplus belongs to the borrower/heirs/beneficiary, and heirs may repay from other resources without forced sale of the property.
